children: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) has developed a standardised and digitally optimised design for 132-kilovolt (kV) substations that reduces execution costs by around 5 million UAE dirhams ($1.36 million) per substation and cuts design and implementation time by more than two months.

Developed by DEWA's Transmission Power division, the design has supported the construction of 90 132kV substations, including 23 commissioned during the first half of 2026, the DFM-listed utility said in a press statement.
The new design approach has also reduced substation components by eliminating around 8,000 electronic parts and 140 kilometres of copper wiring.

Furthermore, optimising the substation layout and footprint in line with digital design reduced the total construction area by 220 square metres (sqm) and saved approximately 12,720 gallons of water annually per substation used for cooling and auxiliary systems.
DEWA said the design has also reduced annual energy consumption by the equivalent of 182 megawatt-hours (MWh) and carbon emissions by approximately 447.24 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually.

“The standardised and digitally optimised design for 132kV substations is not merely an engineering or operational development. Rather, it represents a strategic pillar in Dubai's smart energy transition journey,” said Saeed Mohammed Al Tayer, Managing Director and CEO of DEWA.
He said the design supports efforts to improve grid efficiency, accelerate project delivery and enhance engineering, planning and implementation efficiency as Dubai's electricity demand grows.

Hussain Lootah, Executive Vice President of Transmission Power at DEWA, said the standardised approach facilitates the reuse of approved models in future projects, reducing variations between projects and accelerating workflows from planning through to implementation.
The approach also enables greater integration between engineering and digital components and improves the management of substation data, drawings and technical specifications, he added.
DEWA said the initiative received a six-star rating at the International Best Practice Competition.

title: DEWA's standardised 132kV substation design saves $1.36mln per project
